license_note: Motor performance rows are transcribed from thrustcurve-db 4.0.1 (ISC licence; github.com/broofa/thrustcurve-db, Robert Kieffer), which packages the ThrustCurve.org motor data compiled by John Coker from manufacturer and certification-organisation submissions (NAR S&T, TRA, CAR). The numbers are the manufacturers' own certified figures as published by the certifying body; they are facts about commercial products, reproduced here with attribution under the ISC licence. No value was recalled or invented.

columns.name: common name as a flier says it, e.g. "M1670"
columns.designation: full manufacturer designation as printed on the certification, e.g. "6026M1670-P" — this is what you buy
columns.d_mm: motor diameter, mm (the nominal class, not a measured case OD)
columns.len_mm: overall loaded length, mm, as submitted
columns.case: hardware set the reload fits (joins data/tables/motors.json on mfr|case)
columns.avg_thrust_N: average thrust over the burn, N, certified
columns.max_thrust_N: PEAK thrust, N — the number a retainer, thrust ring, centring ring or bulkhead is loaded by
columns.max_thrust_src: "certified" (the certifying body published it) or "sampled curve (estimate)" (derived here as the maximum of the published thrust-curve samples because the record carries no certified peak)
columns.availability: regular | OOP (out of production), as of the upstream snapshot
columns.curve_samples: number of points in the published thrust curve (0 = no curve in this package)
columns.confidence: likely for a certified peak; recall where the peak had to be derived from the curve
columns.source: the upstream record id and what was transcribed

notes:
WHAT THIS IS FOR. Peak thrust is the load case for every part that carries the motor: a retainer's bolts and its shoulder, a thrust ring, the centring ring that takes thrust into the airframe, an aft bulkhead. The first dry-run retainer had to be TOLD "20 kN peak thrust" because nothing in the app knew it; with this table a request naming a motor carries its certified peak.
LIMITS. (1) These are the manufacturer's certified figures, not a measurement of the motor in your cabinet; a motor fires differently cold. Treat them as nominal and apply the safety factor the part's tier demands. (2) max_thrust_N is certified for 875 of 1037 rows. For the other 162 it is the maximum of the published thrust-curve samples, which is NOT the same number: across the 949 motors carrying both, the curve peak ran from 0.378x to 4.131x the certified peak (median 0.993, 5th-95th percentile 0.719-1.101) because the samples are coarse near ignition. A row whose max_thrust_src is "sampled curve (estimate)" must be declared assumed, and a part designed to it wants margin on top of the usual factor. (3) 7 rows carry a 'disputed' entry: 5 where the recorded peak is below the certified average (impossible, so the peak is withheld — 44 rows in total have no usable peak and a part loaded by one of those motors needs the number from the manufacturer) and 2 where the class letter falls outside the impulse band its name claims. (4) d_mm is the motor's class diameter, not a measured case OD: see data/tables/motors.json for what is and is not known about case dimensions. (5) len_mm is the LOADED length including closures and the protruding nozzle. (6) Availability is the upstream snapshot's; a motor marked OOP may still be in the cabinet and a "regular" one may be unobtainable. (7) Only F and up are here; A-E are in the upstream package but no machined part is designed to them.
JOINS. mfr|case joins data/tables/motors.json (hardware sets: length and mass by grain count). name is what a flier types ("M1670"); designation is what appears on the certification and the vendor's page.
